Split the Deferred row into (1) "Legacy MCP/CLI migration and retirement; generic administration and resource contracts | McpCli, EventStore, FrontComposer and module owners, with Platform for composition and route removal | per AD-11" and (2) "Additional MCP transports including McpCli HTTP, step-up flows, generic mocks, traffic-metric rollback | owning team | outside the MVP; an additional MCP surface or transport needs an AD admitting it under AD-14; forwarded headers never establish the actor".

clusters.title: Incidents after the verification window do not set the promotion stop
clusters.finding: FR-8 (prd.md L208): "An incident establishing that production is no longer working sets or retains the promotion stop until Administrator records a verified baseline." The spine sets the stop only on "every non-working terminal outcome and every DR entry"; the probe only notifies and a failed pre-update health check only stops. Nobody may set the stop outside an attempt.
clusters.scenario: Working release R7 has a latent defect; the probe fails on and off overnight and someone restarts pods; at 09:00 production passes "healthy now", R8 promotes automatically, and R7 stays the rollback target.
clusters.fix: Automatic recovery: "A failed pre-update health check, a probe failure beyond a declared bound, a recorded incident or an Administrator or deputy declaration sets the durable promotion stop; it never triggers an automatic release search. The off-site monitor may set but never clear it."
clusters.notes: RC-13 raised the same PRD obligation; that ID sits in C-05.

clusters.title: The record model is undefined: kinds, writers, cardinality, promotion-stop home and production-promoted lifecycle
clusters.finding: The spine uses six record kinds (release, attempt, three EventStore lifecycle records, Administrator record) with no single statement of writer, timing or location; lifecycle states come from EventStore AD-11, which is never cited and collides with Platform AD-11. Binding classes lists "promotion stop" as an attempt-bound value in "the per-environment attempt record", which is ambiguous: one record per attempt lets a later rotation's working record clear the stop; one mutable record per environment overwrites the last working record that AD-2 must retain. The production-promoted record is written "before traffic" (ambiguous once ingress is open) and is never invalidated when the attempt ends non-working, although EventStore AD-22 consumers treat it as a precondition for removing infrastructure.
clusters.scenario: Builds encodes `promotionStop` in the attempt record, and a rotation rollout's working record silently clears a stop only Administrator may clear. A rolled-back composed host C9 keeps a valid production-promoted record that a legacy-retirement packet cites.
clusters.fix: Rename Binding classes to "Binding classes and records" and define: release record (release-invariant values; publication workflow only; held with the package); attempt records (one per attempt, immutable once terminal; environment executor identity; outside the target cluster and executor host); promotion stop and latest-working pointer as per-environment state with their own set and clear records; lifecycle records (EventStore AD-11 states; EventStore-issued for the server package, Platform-issued for the composed image; production-promoted binds one profile digest); Administrator record (see C-21). Add: "A non-working terminal outcome invalidates the attempt's production-promoted record under EventStore's invalidation rule." Add this to the EventStore confirmation row.

decision.question: When is the production-promoted record written?

options.label: Before the Helm upgrade
options.detail: Write it before the upgrade so no pod serves without it, and invalidate it on any non-working terminal outcome.

options.label: At readiness, before commit
options.detail: Write it once candidate hosts are ready; pods briefly serve without it, and fewer records need invalidating.

clusters.notes: Needs EventStore confirmation (Owned work L314). The store that holds these records is named in C-05.

clusters.title: The grace, timing anchors and takeover are under-specified
clusters.finding: "Grace" appears three times (in-flight retry, interruption detection, replacement-job takeover) without saying whether it is one value, where it is recorded or what its maximum is. Whether a retry that passes inside the grace yields "working" is ambiguous (the PRD says a grace "may finish an in-flight retry"). GitHub never re-runs a job by itself, so takeover "within the grace" is practically unreachable; the lock is not listed among the records kept outside the cluster and executor, and takeover does not say it increments the epoch. "Deployment start" does not say whether catalog preparation and rollback ready-validation fall inside the 10-minute deadline.
clusters.scenario: Check X fails at 4:45 and its retry at 5:15 passes; executor A declares the release working, executor B declares it failed and rolls back.
clusters.fix: "Each attempt records t0 at its first mutation (catalog preparation), the rollout deadline t0 + 10 min, and one attempt grace no longer than the check timeout plus 30 s, used for in-flight retries, interruption detection and takeover. A retry completing within the grace is the check's latest result. The lock and epoch live with the attempt record; a takeover increments the epoch. The maximum lifetime is derived from these values and recorded; an executor dying during verification leaves the lock held and stops for intervention."

clusters.title: Staging data from an unadopted candidate can block every later gate
clusters.finding: Each staging attempt deploys production's baseline onto staging data that holds writes from every earlier candidate, including breaking ones never promoted. AD-15's no-retirement rule is keyed to "recorded working", which staging never reaches. No rule returns staging to a state the baseline can read, and creation tasks run only when a new environment is created.
clusters.scenario: R9 writes an event R7 cannot read; the rehearsal fails and R9 is abandoned; R10's attempt deploys R7, whose projection poisons on R9's events; that is a staging failure, so R10 is blocked, then R11.
clusters.fix: "After a candidate that production does not adopt, staging is returned to a state its production working baseline can read, as its own staging attempt before the next gate. Staging catalog and key retirements follow AD-15 relative to production's working baseline." Record the reset method chosen below.

decision.question: How is staging reset after a candidate that production does not adopt?

options.label: Restore from a staging recovery point
options.detail: Restore staging from a recovery point cut before the abandoned candidate, as its own staging attempt; keeps realistic long-lived data and exercises restore.

options.label: Recreate with synthetic data
options.detail: Recreate staging with its creation tasks and synthetic data; simpler and deterministic, but loses long-lived data realism.

clusters.title: The planned recovery for an approved incompatible release has no execution rules
clusters.finding: Release modes lets an incompatible release run in Administrator-approved mode with "the separately planned recovery that replaces automatic rollback", but does not say whether the executor runs it in the same job and lock, stops with user ingress open or closed, or treats a data-restoring plan as a DR entry. No recovery point is required right before the attempt. The PRD also requires the approval to name the recovery procedure "and its acceptance checks before the attempt" (prd.md L48, L168); the spine has neither part.
clusters.scenario: R12 (breaking schema) is approved at 18:00 with the plan "restore the pre-release backup"; verification fails at 18:12; the newest complete recovery point is from 17:31; the executor stops, Administrator is unreachable, users write under R12 until morning, and the plan loses everything since 17:31.
clusters.fix: Release modes: "... whose record names, before the attempt, the separately planned recovery and its acceptance checks." Add the execution rule chosen below.

decision.question: How does a failed approved incompatible release recover?

options.label: Recovery point, stop, then DR-entry recovery
options.detail: The attempt starts only after a complete recovery point cut after the lock; on a non-working outcome the executor sets the stop, closes user ingress and stops; the named recovery runs as a DR entry under a new epoch by Administrator or the deputy, with the same verification.

options.label: Executor runs the plan in-job
options.detail: The executor runs the planned recovery automatically in the same job and lock; faster, but automates a data restore with no human check.

clusters.title: The rollback generation's content and the recovery render are mis-specified
clusters.finding: The rollback generation holds "the baseline's routes plus every still-referenced idempotency and key entry", evaluated at preparation, before smoke writes create records for candidate-only command C. EventStore AD-25 refuses retirement while records remain, so the rollback commit fails, and every rehearsal "exercising at least one idempotent command new in the candidate" becomes breaking. The recovery render reads environment-current catalog generations, which after commit is the candidate's, so baseline hosts fail readiness and the single recovery is spent.
clusters.scenario: Every release that adds an idempotent command is classified breaking; or automatic recovery renders the baseline with the candidate generation and fails.
clusters.fix: "The rollback generation contains every idempotency and key entry of both the baseline and the candidate generations, with candidate-only entries as retention entries, fixed at preparation. Recovery mirrors activation: the baseline render carries the prepared rollback generation, committed at readiness." Confirm with EventStore (already a deferred confirmation).

clusters.title: "Breaking" is defined in five places, and the module-facing rule is hidden in AD-3
clusters.finding: Module declaration (none/additive/breaking), Module intake (effective = maximum), AD-3 ("Previous code must read current schemas and events with current security state"), AD-15 (additive only when the baseline tolerates it), Production profile ("otherwise the change is breaking") and Staging gate (a failed rehearsal is breaking evidence) each define part of "breaking".
clusters.scenario: An agent classifying a Parties release reads Module declaration and Module intake, never reaches AD-3 or AD-15, and marks as additive a change the baseline cannot read.
clusters.fix: Make Module intake the single definition: "A module release is breaking when its predecessor cannot read the state, events and security state it writes (AD-3), when the baseline host cannot tolerate its adapter or descriptor changes (AD-15), or when its staging rehearsal fails; otherwise additive, or none when no release-owned object changed." The other homes say "(breaking per Module intake)".
clusters.notes: The pragmatism lens asked to confirm the trigger list; the updater should check it against C-15 (forward-only inputs) and C-16 (qualified sets) when applying. Treated as autofix because it is a confirmation, not a trade-off.

clusters.title: Observability has no environment-isolation or failure-domain rule, and its gate is late
clusters.finding: Diagnostics says only "Use shared technical-module health and telemetry". The sink, OTLP path and per-environment separation are undecided and gated "before G2" inside the recovery row, although staging E2E diagnostics need a sink at the first staging deployment. Default-deny egress means Platform must render the export destination. Nothing requires production diagnostics to outlive the node, which PRD FR-8 requires.
clusters.scenario: Staging and production export to one in-cluster collector and staging-authorized people read production traces with tenant data; or one module declares the collector as egress and the others are silently blocked; an in-cluster sink loses the logs that would explain a node failure.
clusters.fix: Diagnostics: "Telemetry sinks are per environment, or partitioned with production data readable only by production principals. Platform renders exporter configuration and egress; modules never declare the sink. Attempt-window diagnostics and production telemetry needed for incident analysis are shipped outside the primary failure domain with the declared minimum retention." Gate the sink before the first staging deployment; keep retention and off-site durability before G2.
clusters.notes: OPS-16 proposed defer; it is folded in as wording.

clusters.title: WorkflowAccessPolicy is alpha, matches callers by app ID only, and is open until a policy is loaded
clusters.finding: AD-8: "Hosted Dapr Configurations and WorkflowAccessPolicies deny by default and allow callers by trust domain, namespace and app ID." In Dapr 1.18.4 WorkflowAccessPolicy is `dapr.io/v1alpha1`; `WorkflowCaller` has only `AppID`; there is no `defaultAction`; calls are allowed while no policy is loaded for a target; cross-namespace workflows are unsupported. The CRD is installed live with zero policies.
clusters.scenario: Implementers cannot express the mandated triple match; deny-by-default holds only if every workflow-hosting app has a scoped policy; the alpha API changes between minors unnoticed.
clusters.fix: "Configurations match by trust domain, namespace and app ID. WorkflowAccessPolicies match by app ID within the single-namespace workflow scope, and every workflow-hosting app has at least one scoped policy." Add "Dapr WorkflowAccessPolicy v1alpha1" to the accepted prerelease risks, and a negative test that a staging app ID equal to a production app ID cannot schedule production workflows.

clusters.title: Dapr patch pinning, sidecar skew and HotReload posture are undefined
clusters.finding: Dapr 1.18 HotReload is GA and on by default: Component and Subscription changes reload in place; Configuration, Resiliency, WorkflowAccessPolicy and HTTPEndpoint changes gracefully restart every sidecar that loads them; actor-state-store reload behavior changed between 1.18.2 and 1.18.3, inside the observed skew. The spine records none of this. "Within the control plane's supported skew" is not an upstream term (Dapr defines minor support and upgrade paths only). "One sidecar patch per release across local, CI and staging" (memlog V-47) makes every developer and agent sandbox track release patches.
clusters.scenario: A Helm upgrade that changes an application-package Dapr resource restarts baseline sidecars before candidate readiness, breaking the assumption that the baseline serves during catalog activation; a shared Configuration change restarts sidecars at once and trips the 60-second unavailability rule; environment-layer Component changes propagate the moment they are applied.
clusters.fix: Define skew: "Hosted sidecar patch equals the control-plane patch; CI and staging control-plane and sidecar images equal the release's pinned patch." Pin the exact Dapr patch in the profile template; add HotReload behavior to the Aspire-to-Helm qualification and the rollback rehearsal. Record the option chosen below.

decision.question: How are Dapr runtime changes controlled in hosted and local environments?

options.label: HotReload off, exact patch, local warns
options.detail: Disable HotReload in hosted Configurations so Dapr resource changes follow pod rollout; pin the exact patch per release across CI, staging and production; local runs report their patch and warn on mismatch.

options.label: HotReload on, modelled
options.detail: Keep HotReload and model its restarts in the rollout, rollback and verification rules; local runs warn only.

options.label: Keep V-47 as written
options.detail: Enforce the release patch on local runs too and keep HotReload off; strictest, and burdens every developer and agent sandbox.

clusters.notes: Related to C-16's sidecar-patch binding.

clusters.title: The Aspire Kubernetes publisher renders connection strings into Secrets and Helm values
clusters.finding: AD-1: "In hosted publish, data services become external connection parameters." Aspire maps connection strings and environment variables to ConfigMaps and Secrets, parameters become Helm values, and Helm keeps release values in an in-cluster release Secret. The Secrets convention allows Kubernetes Secrets only as documented bootstrap exceptions, and AD-8 keeps bootstrap Secrets outside the application deploy identity's scope. The Aspire-to-Helm qualification row omits this check (V-38 raised it earlier).
clusters.scenario: Database and broker credentials passed as connection parameters land in application-namespace Secrets and in Helm release history, managed by the application deploy identity.
clusters.fix: "Hosted connection parameters carry only non-secret endpoints; credentials resolve through Dapr secret stores or component `secretKeyRef`." Add "the rendered chart contains no credential-bearing Secret or values" to the Aspire-to-Helm qualification.

clusters.title: AD-8's negative-test list does not bind the NFR-3 matrix
clusters.finding: AD-8 names data services, app ports, sidecars, workflows, actors, volumes and hostnames. NFR-3 also requires secret access (the production OpenBao), identity administration (the staging management client and staging admins against the production realm; McpCli tokens against the admin API), automation credentials (staging executor identities against production namespaces, environment-layer objects, registry writes, records and evidence, backup prefixes and the internal verification endpoint), restored copies, and denial after revocation. PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped, so "volumes in the data namespace" is not a boundary.
clusters.scenario: A qualification suite passes AD-8's list while a staging executor credential can still read production backup prefixes.
clusters.fix: Replace the AD-8 list with NFR-3's categories plus secrets, identity administration, automation credentials, restored copies, PV binding and post-revocation denial after every admission change. "PVs are created only by the production shared-infrastructure identity and are pre-bound to their environment's claims."

clusters.title: Composed-host deliverables are gated on Folders, and a one-time ratification is written into AD-13
clusters.finding: AD-13 makes the Platform-composed `eventstore` host mandatory in every environment, and hosted deployments need Platform-issued lifecycle records, which depend on EventStore registering Platform as composed-subject issuer. EventStore still binds its own `eventstore` release mapping and has no extension API or issuer registration. The owned-work row gates the composed host "before Folders joins a Platform environment", while the representative Aspire-to-Helm composition (Parties with EventStore, Tenants and Memories) needs a composed image first. AD-13 also contains a one-time process step ("EventStore ratifies this rule once, registering Platform as issuer"), repeated in the source row and the owned-work row.
clusters.scenario: The epic plan schedules the composed host with Folders; the first staging deployment uses EventStore's stock image, violating AD-13 and lacking valid Platform-issued records, or blocks unexpectedly.
clusters.fix: Re-gate: "Composed host build (with zero or more extensions), its lifecycle-subject registration and EventStore's issuer ratification: before the first staging deployment. Folders adapter packaging: before Folders joins." Move the ratification into First shared versions ("AD-13 ratification and composed-subject issuer registration | EventStore | Platform | composed host release-available") and delete it from AD-13 and the EventStore row.

clusters.title: Provenance chain gaps: module images unattested, predicate inconsistent, transitive actions tag-pinned
clusters.finding: The publication workflow "verifies the intake-pinned module images" and "Provenance for each artifact class names its caller repository, workflow, protected ref and pinned Builds workflow ref", but no module release attests its images: Builds `domain-release` attests only `*.nupkg`, EventStore has no image attestation, and Memories uses Builds actions at `@main` with no attestation. The expected signer identity per module is recorded nowhere. AD-2 and Workflows list different provenance fields. `gh attestation verify` has no flag for the caller workflow file, which lives in the Fulcio Build Config URI. Only "SHA-pinned Builds reusable workflows" is bound; Builds composite actions pin `docker/login-action`, `setup-dotnet` and `NuGet/login` by tag. Nothing stops the publication push credential from deleting or overwriting retained artifacts.
clusters.scenario: The publication workflow cannot verify any Memories or EventStore image, so every release blocks, or verification quietly degrades to a digest pin; a naive verifier accepts artifacts from any Platform workflow that calls the pinned Builds workflow; a retagged third-party action exfiltrates the registry push credential before attestation.
clusters.fix: Make Workflows and provenance the single home (AD-2 points to it). Predicate: "signer workflow and digest, source repository and ref, and Build Config URI equal to the publication workflow path; for module images, an attestation naming the module repository, workflow, protected ref and pinned Builds workflow ref, recorded per module in the intake manifest." Add: "The full uses closure of publication and deployment workflows is SHA- or digest-pinned and checked by the Builds governed closure. Publication credentials cannot delete or overwrite retained artifacts; the replica has a separate writer." Owned-work row: Builds `domain-release` attests image digests; EventStore and Memories adopt it or an equivalent attested path; before the first staging promotion.

clusters.title: The registry is anonymously readable, a second registry exists, and the composed image name collides with EventStore's
clusters.finding: Anonymous `GET https://registry.hexalith.com/v2/_catalog` and tag lists succeed (Zot v2.1.20); a separate private Zot serves `registry.tache.ai`; the `eventstore` repository holds EventStore-published tags 3.100.0 to 3.104.0. Workflows says "pull credentials are per-environment secrets", which adds no read control, and does not say which registry holds retained artifacts. AD-13's composed `eventstore` image collides with the existing EventStore repository.
clusters.scenario: The composed-image subject is confused with EventStore's stock image; per-environment pull credentials are built as a control that controls nothing.
clusters.fix: Name the retained-artifact registry and its read policy; name the composed-image repository distinctly (for example `platform/eventstore`) or state that EventStore's `eventstore` repository is not a deployment subject; add Zot to the currency row.

decision.question: Is the retained-artifact registry publicly readable?

clusters.title: The NFR-2 response-coverage rule is loose
clusters.finding: Detection and response: "declares response arrangements, such as staffed hours and a maximum acknowledgement time; the RTO is assessed within them". NFR-2 (prd.md L297-301) fixes coverage with a time zone, primary/deputy responsibility and a maximum acknowledgement delay; an incident that begins within coverage stays covered when coverage ends; the clock never pauses or restarts; every incident records full duration and coverage status. The PRD review (A-1) asks the spine to carry this so implementation uses one definition; "such as" makes each element optional.
clusters.scenario: The drill-report builder counts an incident that began 10 minutes before coverage ended as covered, while the incident-report builder pauses the clock outside coverage; the RTO evidence is incompatible.
clusters.fix: "The recovery procedure publishes response coverage with its time zone, primary and deputy responsibility and maximum acknowledgement time. The four-hour RTO applies to outages beginning within coverage and stays applicable when coverage ends mid-incident; outside coverage no four-hour commitment is made. Every incident records original outage time, coverage status and full outage-to-verified-restoration duration; the clock never pauses or restarts."

clusters.title: The post-DR handover and degraded posture are undefined
clusters.finding: The recovery executor writes the DR attempt record that becomes the working baseline, but AD-2 accepts attempt records "only from the environment's executor identity"; the production executor's credentials are revoked in DR step 1 and it cannot reach the replacement API; the recovery executor refuses routine workflows. On a single node DR also loses staging, and the prepared capacity becomes production, so no staging exists for the mandatory gate, no prepared capacity remains (a G2 precondition), and the monitor may have been hosted on the consumed capacity.
clusters.scenario: The first attempt after DR stops on an unaccepted baseline; two days later a security fix cannot be promoted because staging no longer exists; a second failure has no prepared target.
clusters.fix: "The recovery executor is an accepted attempt-record writer for DR attempts. DR step 6 re-provisions the production executor's allowlist and credentials for the replacement capacity, recorded in the DR attempt before promotion resumes. After DR, production runs in a recorded degraded posture: new prepared capacity is identified, a drill repeats as a material change, and Administrator records the return to G2 conditions." Add the promotion rule chosen below.

decision.question: Can anything be promoted while staging is gone after DR?

options.label: Stop until staging returns
options.detail: The promotion stop stays set until staging is re-established; urgent fixes wait for staging.

options.label: Approved emergency mode with a temporary staging
options.detail: Allow an Administrator-approved emergency release rehearsed on a temporary staging on spare capacity during the degraded posture.

clusters.title: Custody classes converge on the persistent recovery executor
clusters.finding: Restoring needs read access to ciphertext backups, decryption material, the tenant-key backup and prepared-capacity credentials, and all of it meets on one long-lived off-site host that runs monthly drills. Nothing binds per-job release of custody material, rotation after drills or DR, no write or delete on recovery points, provenance checks on pulled artifacts, or a destruction bound for drill and quarantine copies (which are erasure targets). This undoes AD-12's separation.
clusters.scenario: An attacker persists on the recovery executor between drills and captures decrypted production data and tenant keys during the next monthly drill.
clusters.fix: "The recovery executor holds standing credentials only for the prepared capacity, plus read-only access to recovery points. Custodians release key and decryption material per job, destroyed at job end. Credentials rotate after every drill and DR. Restored artifacts are provenance-verified, with attestations replicated. Drill and quarantine copies are erasure targets and are destroyed with verification within a stated bound."

clusters.title: A complete recovery point omits tenant-key coverage and event-export lag
clusters.finding: "Complete" does not require a tenant-key backup that covers every key generation referenced at or before the cut, and tenant-key backups have no stated cadence. Keycloak event-export "freshness" has no bound, so revocations after the last shipment are lost in DR step 4.
clusters.scenario: Tenant T is created at 10:05; the key backup runs daily at 00:30; the 10:30 data cut is reported complete; the node is lost at 10:50, and T's data is restored as ciphertext without its key.
clusters.fix: "A recovery point is complete only when a tenant-key backup covers every key generation referenced at or before its cut; the monitor verifies this without holding key material. The Keycloak event export ships within a declared bound, and its lag is monitored like recovery-point age."

clusters.title: The drill cannot prove the RTO as written
clusters.finding: "Measures real detection" contradicts "never mutate live production". Substitutions (fence against copies, Keycloak generated from the contract, no DNS or certificate cutover, a mirror copy) are listed but untimed. Rebuild-only replay (Memories syntactic, vector and graph projections, possibly re-embedded) is on the critical path with no rule on whether reopening waits for it. Monthly drills occupy the prepared capacity, and nothing says a real disaster preempts a drill.
clusters.scenario: The drill reports 2 h 40 min; the real event adds DNS propagation, ACME issuance, a Keycloak restore of both realms and a 5-hour Memories re-projection, about 9 hours to verified service.
clusters.fix: "Detection time is the probe interval plus the measured probe-to-issue latency against a drill target. Each substitution records a measured or bounded duration for the real step, added to the RTO; an unbounded substitution fails the RTO proof. Each module declares whether reopening waits for its rebuild-only replay or admits a declared degraded state, and the drill times it at representative size. A real DR entry aborts any running drill and reclaims the prepared capacity."

clusters.title: Build-substrate findability: undefined terms, an AD-only capability map, single-paragraph Rules and rationale inside Rules
clusters.finding: Terms are used before they are defined or never defined: release-invariant, working baseline and environment-current before Binding classes; G1-G3 from AD-9 on; SM-4/SM-5 never; evidence-validated, release-available and production-promoted never. Foreign AD numbers collide with Platform ones (EventStore AD-10/AD-11). The capability map lists ADs only, so enrolling Parties touches 13 locations with no entry point. Rules average about 180-200 words (AD-11 247-290, AD-7 216-251), and several bundle four to six sub-rules. Rationale fragments remain in Rules ("Because `azp` authenticates only confidential clients", "`--rollback-on-failure` (formerly `--atomic`)", "co-scheduling ... is the AD-8 residual risk"). The DR sequence is a numbered list inside a table cell, and the attempt lifecycle is a state machine spread across six prose rows.
clusters.scenario: A small agent opening AD-2 cold cannot resolve its terms; one reads AD-14's "because" clause as a condition; another misses the takeover transition in Attempt ownership.
clusters.fix: Add a ~70-word Terms paragraph after Roles (unprefixed AD-n means this spine; PRD glossary terms, G1-G3 and SM-n apply; record kinds per Binding classes and records; lifecycle states are EventStore AD-11's) and prefix foreign AD numbers with the module name. Add convention and R&R row names to the capability map's governing column. Render long Rules as three to six labelled sub-bullets; move the DR sequence out of the table cell into a numbered list; group Module declaration fields. Move the three rationale fragments to the memlog. Optionally add one attempt-lifecycle diagram (the PR-112 sketch) after the record-timing decision in C-35.

clusters.title: The realm contract omits token-exchange preconditions, and the memlog's Keycloak version is stale
clusters.finding: Keycloak 26.7.4 standard token exchange requires the requester client in the subject token's `aud`, a per-client "Standard token exchange" switch, and issues no refresh token by default. The realm contract lists none of these. The installed Keycloak digest resolves to 26.7.4 (current), but the memlog still says the version is unknown.
clusters.scenario: Without audience mappers, the gateway-to-module-to-module exchange chain fails at runtime.
clusters.fix: Add the audience, per-client switch and refresh-token settings to the realm-contract First shared versions row; record the 26.7.4 observation and drop the Keycloak currency open item.

clusters.title: The synthetic-tenant flag has no owning shape that aggregators can read
clusters.finding: Synthetic identities: "one pre-provisioned, flagged synthetic tenant per environment ... synthetic data stays out of real-tenant views and aggregates". The tenant-level flag has no owner or shape (a Tenants attribute, a realm-contract value or a Platform list). Projects' rolling aggregates and Memories access telemetry consume events keyed by tenant, not tokens.
clusters.scenario: Aggregators cannot exclude smoke writes and pollute SM-7/SM-8, or each module invents its own marker.
clusters.fix: "The synthetic tenant identifier per environment is published in the environment descriptor and the realm-contract instance, and EventStore attests it on admitted events; modules exclude by that identifier."
